Orbit GeometryMath.cpp adapts only the double-precision atan and atan2
kernels from OpenLibm's src/s_atan.c and src/e_atan2.c, originally developed
by Sun Microsystems as fdlibm. No complete math library is bundled.

Pinned source and source checksums are recorded in source.lock.json.
The original permission notices are preserved in LICENSE.txt and in the
adapted source.

Local changes:
- Internal orbit::detail namespace; no replacement of process-wide libm.
- C++ fixed-width types and memcpy bit access instead of C word macros.
- Explicit const-volatile reads without casting away const.
- Equivalent exponent-difference comparisons without signed right shifts.
- No weak aliases, exported C math symbols, or platform header dependency.
- Fixed polynomial operation order, no fast math or multiply-add contraction.

Graphic-eye angle-weighted normals and crescent socket angles use these
kernels. Float socket angles explicitly round the double result to float.
The shared result is included in the geometry compiler and fit-profile
identity.
